findings.issue_text: [High/bug] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — The client-side size check hardcodes `10 * 1024`, discarding `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`. Admin-configured limits are silently ignored: if `max_image_size_kb` is raised above 10MB, the client now rejects images the server would accept/downsize (so the feature itself only works up to 10MB); if lowered, no client pre-screening occurs; and the "file_too_large" alert always claims the max is 10240 KB regardless of configuration.

[Medium/bug] app/models/optimized_image.rb:142-152 — `downsize` is defined twice in the resulting file; the second definition (`from, to, dimensions, opts`) silently overrides the first at class load, making the first (whose body was even updated) dead code. Any caller still using the old `(from, to, max_width, max_height)` signature will have an Integer passed as `dimensions`/`opts`, crashing or generating wrong convert instructions — a breaking internal API change.

[Medium/bug] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:63-70 — There is no size re-check after the downsize loop. Each pass only cuts pixel area to ~64%, so images more than ~3x `max_image_size_kb` (or any image where conversion fails) are still uploaded oversized — `max_image_size_kb` is no longer a hard cap, contradicting the "reduced to allowed size" comment.

[Medium/bug] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — `allow_animation:` can never take effect on this path: `tempfile.path` (RackMultipart and `FileHelper.download` tempfiles) has no file extension, so `from =~ /\.GIF$/i` in `OptimizedImage.optimize` never matches and the `_animated` instructions are never selected; oversized animated GIFs are downsized via the non-animated path.

[Medium/performance] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:63-70 — Up to 5 sequential ImageMagick conversions run synchronously inside the web request on files up to 10MB, blocking the worker for seconds per upload; any user can trivially repeat this, creating a CPU/memory exhaustion (DoS) vector.

[Low/bug] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — The boolean return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize` is ignored: on conversion failure (corrupt file, missing ImageMagick) the identical failing conversion is retried up to 5 times and the original file is then uploaded with no error surfaced.

[Medium/test_gap] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:63 / app/models/optimized_image.rb — No tests were added or updated for the new downsizing loop (success, non-image bypass, still-too-large-after-5-passes, API URL path) or for the changed `OptimizedImage.downsize` signature; existing 4-arg callers/specs would break unnoticed.

[Low/bug] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246 — The 413 handler now always reports a 10MB limit, but the actual cause is the web server's `client_max_body_size` (or the site setting), so users are shown an incorrect maximum size.

[Low/security] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — `FileHelper.download`'s size cap is hardcoded to `10.megabytes` instead of deriving from a site setting; for API-supplied URLs the server will now fetch up to 10MB regardless of the configured `max_image_size_kb`, increasing the fetch/SSRF resource footprint with no admin control.

[Low/data] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — Fixed "80%" per-pass downsizing over-shrinks images only marginally over the limit (a single pass cuts pixel area ~36%) and compounds generational re-encode quality loss across passes; the scale factor should be computed from the actual reduction needed.

goldens.comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:63-70 — There is no size re-check after the downsize loop. Each pass only cuts pixel area to ~64%, so images more than ~3x `max_image_size_kb` (or any image where conversion fails) are still uploaded oversized — `max_image_size_kb` is no longer a hard cap, contradicting the "reduced to allowed size" comment.

adjudication.rationale: The new downsize loop in `uploads_controller.rb` (lines added around `while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`) will stop after 5 attempts even if the tempfile is still larger than `max_image_size_kb`, and it does not check the final size or handle a downsize failure before calling `Upload.create_for(...)`. That’s a concrete, diff-grounded gap vs the comment “reduced to allowed size”. However, from this diff alone we can’t verify whether `Upload.create_for` (or model validations) still enforces the hard cap and rejects oversized uploads, so it’s not provably a functional bug based only on the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — `allow_animation:` can never take effect on this path: `tempfile.path` (RackMultipart and `FileHelper.download` tempfiles) has no file extension, so `from =~ /\.GIF$/i` in `OptimizedImage.optimize` never matches and the `_animated` instructions are never selected; oversized animated GIFs are downsized via the non-animated path.

adjudication.rationale: In the new upload resize loop, `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, ...)` passes the tempfile *path* as `from`, and `OptimizedImage.optimize` selects animated instructions only when `opts[:allow_animation]` and `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`. The diff shows this decision is based solely on the filesystem path, not on `filename`/content-type. For the API URL path, the tempfile is created via `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, "discourse-upload-#{type}")`, which (as written) does not include a `.gif` suffix, so animated-GIF detection can fail and the non-animated instruction set would be used when downsizing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/performance] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:63-70 — Up to 5 sequential ImageMagick conversions run synchronously inside the web request on files up to 10MB, blocking the worker for seconds per upload; any user can trivially repeat this, creating a CPU/memory exhaustion (DoS) vector.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds synchronous image downsizing inside `UploadsController#create_upload` (new loop at lines ~63-70) that can run up to 5 `OptimizedImage.downsize` calls per request while `tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`. `OptimizedImage.downsize` ultimately executes ImageMagick via backticks in `convert_with`, so this work happens inline on the web request thread/process. Since this path is reachable for any user uploading an image (no admin check) and the code also increases client/server-side allowed size to 10MB in multiple places, it plausibly enables CPU/memory exhaustion by repeated large uploads. This is a concrete security/performance defect introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — The boolean return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize` is ignored: on conversion failure (corrupt file, missing ImageMagick) the identical failing conversion is retried up to 5 times and the original file is then uploaded with no error surfaced.

adjudication.rationale: In the new downsizing loop in `uploads_controller.rb`, `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` is called up to 5 times but its return value is ignored. From `optimized_image.rb`, `convert_with` returns `false` on failure (and `nil` on success), so a conversion failure won’t be detected; the loop will keep retrying as long as `tempfile.size` remains above the limit, which is likely if conversion fails. However, the claim that the oversized original is then uploaded “with no error surfaced” is not verifiable from this diff because `Upload.create_for(...)` may still enforce size limits and produce errors.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:63 / app/models/optimized_image.rb — No tests were added or updated for the new downsizing loop (success, non-image bypass, still-too-large-after-5-passes, API URL path) or for the changed `OptimizedImage.downsize` signature; existing 4-arg callers/specs would break unnoticed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces nontrivial new behavior in `UploadsController#create_upload` (a 5-try downsizing loop gated on `FileHelper.is_image?`, size checks, and different paths for API URL downloads vs direct uploads) and also changes `OptimizedImage.downsize` to effectively take a single `dimensions` argument (the later `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` overrides the earlier 4-arg version). No test/spec files are modified in this diff, so coverage for these new branches and the signature change is not demonstrated here; this is a concrete, diff-grounded test gap concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246 — The 413 handler now always reports a 10MB limit, but the actual cause is the web server's `client_max_body_size` (or the site setting), so users are shown an incorrect maximum size.

adjudication.rationale: The diff hardcodes `maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024` in the JS 413 handler (`utilities.js`), whereas previously it used `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`. Since 413 is described in-code as "usually returned from the web server," the actual limit could differ from 10MB (server body-size limit or the site setting). This change can therefore show users an incorrect maximum size in the error message.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/security] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — `FileHelper.download`'s size cap is hardcoded to `10.megabytes` instead of deriving from a site setting; for API-supplied URLs the server will now fetch up to 10MB regardless of the configured `max_image_size_kb`, increasing the fetch/SSRF resource footprint with no admin control.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the API URL download cap from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a hardcoded `10.megabytes` in `uploads_controller.rb` (`FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)`). This removes admin-configurable control over how much data the server will fetch for API-supplied URLs and can increase the maximum fetched content size beyond the configured limit, expanding SSRF/DoS resource impact. The new downsize loop happens only after the download, so it does not mitigate the larger fetch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/data] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — Fixed "80%" per-pass downsizing over-shrinks images only marginally over the limit (a single pass cuts pixel area ~36%) and compounds generational re-encode quality loss across passes; the scale factor should be computed from the actual reduction needed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a loop in `uploads_controller.rb` that repeatedly calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` while the tempfile’s *bytesize* exceeds `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` (up to 5 passes). This fixed 80% scaling per pass is not computed from how far over the size limit the image is, so images only slightly above the limit can be reduced much more than necessary, and repeated re-encoding can compound quality loss. This is a concrete, diff-grounded algorithm/quality concern rather than a clear correctness failure.
